title: Legal Writing II: appellate advocacy and drafting
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Write persuasive motions and briefs, use the standard of review and the record, structure and deliver an oral argument, and draft contracts and other transactional documents clearly.
primary_reading: Cornell LII: Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure

weeks.2: Theory of the case and themes
weeks.4: Standards of review and the record
weeks.6: The statement of the case and facts
weeks.12: Drafting for clarity: ambiguity and boilerplate

blocks.deliverable: Rewrite an objective memo section persuasively.
Draft point headings for a three-issue brief.
Write a persuasive statement of facts from a supplied record.
Week 7 midterm; draft a motion with a supporting memorandum.
Prepare and deliver a 10-minute oral argument outline.
Draft the core provisions of a services agreement.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Appellate brief: from a record and authorities supplied in the project, write a 3,500-word appellate brief for one side and an oral argument outline with anticipated questions.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
